independent_reasoning: The actual global-ODE supplier already depends on the conservation theorem and records it as its own F2, but that hidden proof context should not be attributed to a stronger advertised global-ODE Statement. Promoting the exact conservation supplier to a direct dependency removes the mismatch cleanly.

The existing conservation theorem advertises constant sum_i x_i n_i(t)+L(t) for every nonnegative event-ODE solution as long as it exists. Its actual Proof3.1 proves this by pairing each finite event increment with the augmented mass vector: in-range coagulation preserves parent sum through fixed-pivot barycentric identities, overflow transfers the exact lost mass to L, and fragmentation daughter first moment equals parent mass. Summing finite zero-mass increments gives the zero mass derivative, then constant initial mass. Its positivity proof and event assumptions match the exact solution supplied by the global-ODE theorem.

Apply that conservation result to the unique global nonnegative solution with initial mass M. Since every grid pivot x_i is positive, its simplex S_M is closed and bounded, hence compact in finite dimension; it contains the initial state, so it is nonempty even when M=0. The already direct forward-Euler positivity/conservation theorem puts each successful numerical state into the same S_M under the existing CFL condition.

Consequently the existing Proof1.1 is licensed unchanged: polynomial F has bounded norm on S_M, h<=T bounds exact-start Euler outputs by R_S+TB_F, and the enlarged compact tube has positive margin inside its open convex-fiber cylinder. Polynomial F and its derivatives are bounded on that bounded cylinder. The actual local-error supplier gives uniform Ch^2 defects and1+Lh stability; the actual global-error supplier then gives C_T h with zero initial error. The constant is independent of N and the convergence remains only to this finite-dimensional event ODE.

No new local conservation proof item, supplier Statement change, new axiom, weaker box-only replacement or loss of the richer mass-simplex argument is necessary. This repair uses an already present proved exact supplier and leaves every original target claim intact.
